title: Pin Terraform modules with lockfile and add Helm chart controlplane provisioner
author: Michael Chen
description: Motivation: We need deterministic and auditable private control plane provisioning for customers deploying Redwood Private. This change pins external Terraform module versions via a repository-level lockfile, introduces a light Helm chart provisioner that the installer uses to create control-plane Kubernetes primitives, and wires end-to-end CI/e2e checks so module changes do not silently break subnet/endpoint creation. Summary: 1) Add terraform.lock.hcl at the installer root with exact provider/module checksums and update CI to validate lockfile consistency. 2) Introduce a small Helm chart (helm/controlplane-provisioner) used by the installer in the 'plan' stage to render Job manifests that run subnet assignment and endpoint creation logic. 3) Add migration helper scripts (scripts/migrate/controlplane-subnet-migrate.sh) to perform atomic subnet handoffs with pre/post DNS stamps and a safe rollback marker. 4) Update Terraform modules usage to a pinned source and bumped module inputs for conditional Privatelink provisioning. 5) Add a rollback-ready flag and a reconciliation worker toggle that can be enabled via installer config. Why this is different: prior PRs have focused on subnet allocation or DNS stitching in isolation; this PR ties module version management and chart-driven provisioning together so a module update cannot be applied without CI ensuring the corresponding Helm chart and migration path exist. Checklist: - [x] Add terraform.lock.hcl and CI check - [x] Add helm/controlplane-provisioner chart skeleton and simple templated Job - [x] Wire installer to use Helm chart during apply (chart rendered in dry-run for customers) - [x] Add migration script with idempotent mark-and-sweep step - [x] Add e2e smoke test that simulates a small subnet reallocation and DNS stamp validation - [x] Document operator-facing rollback steps in docs/installer/upgrade-readme.md How to validate locally: run ./scripts/dev/with-kind.sh then ./scripts/migrate/controlplane-subnet-migrate.sh --dry-run --stamp=ci-test; run terraform init && terraform validate --lockfile=readonly CI notes: The change adds a new pipeline stage 'lockfile-verify' that fails if terraform.lock.hcl is out of sync, and an e2e stage that deploys the helm chart into a ephemeral cluster. Tests flaked once on first run (helm timeout), fixed by increasing probe timeouts. Rollout plan: squash-merge into main, monitor canary customer namespaces for 48h (feature gated by toggle), then flip reconciliation worker to on by default after 72h if no regressions observed.

feat(helm): add controlplane-provisioner chart with templated job and rbac
refactor(installer): wire helm chart render path into apply flow
ci: add lockfile-verify and e2e helm deploy stages

release_notes: Pin Terraform modules with repository lockfile; introduce Helm-based controlplane provisioner used by the installer; add migration and rollback tooling for safe subnet handoffs; CI verifies lockfile and runs E2E helm deploy.
notes_for_ops: After merge: 1) Ensure CI secret with registry credentials is present for the e2e job. 2) Enable feature gate 'helm_controlplane_provisioner' in tenant config for canary customers. 3) Monitor DNS stamp metrics and reconciliation worker logs for any unexpected 5xx. 4) If rollback needed, follow docs/installer/upgrade-readme.md -> 'Rollback to previous module version' which uses the tombstone marker flow.
risk_assessment: medium: introduces new installer flow and migration script; changes are behind a feature toggle and CI gate. Rollback path implemented.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for marker handling and Helm rendering; e2e smoke test deploys provisioner into kind cluster, runs subnet migration in dry-run, and validates DNS entries via mocked route53. CI passed after one retries due to Helm probe timeout which was increased.
